title: Lesson 13: Focused Read-aloud and Retelling, Session 2: Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky
objective: Students will retell major events and describe the central message of the story Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky through listening, discussion, role-play, and writing activities.

what_is_taught.skill: retell major events from a story
describe the central message of a story
use text illustrations to support understanding of story events
participate in partner discussions to share and expand ideas
use sentence frames or prompts to support oral language production
write responses about story events and central message
use classroom resources (e.g., story elements board, word walls) to support writing

what_is_NOT_taught: advanced vocabulary instruction beyond story context

student_actions.oral_production: participate in partner discussions, share ideas aloud, role-play story events, and self-assess learning orally
student_actions.written_production: write responses on the Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky response sheet
student_actions.matching_sorting_sequencing: sequence story events by placing icons on the Story Elements board and ordering story chunks
student_actions.procedural_application: apply the Sit, Kneel, Stand self-assessment protocol
student_actions.investigation_handson: manipulate puppets to role-play story events
student_actions.representation_modeling: model motions for the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song and Moon Movement routine
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain how story events support understanding of the central message and give examples
student_actions.comprehension_response: answer questions about story events and central message during read-aloud and discussions with partners and whole group; reflect on learning progress

evidence.quote: Invite students to sing and move along to the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song with you.
Refocus the group and guide the class through the Moon Movement routine using the Moon Movement chart.
I can retell major events from Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky.
I can describe the central message of Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky.

Display Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky and remind students to use the signal, as in previous lessons, to show when they see or hear an important event from the beginning, middle, and end of the story.

Draw students' attention back to the text and read aloud pages 1-13 slowly, fluently, with expression, and without interruption, paying attention to when students show the signal for an important event.

'What did you hear that helped you understand the important events from the beginning of the story?' (Sun wants Water to visit his and Moon's house, but Water says the house is too small for all of his people. Sun and Moon decide to build a larger house.)
'What did you see in the illustrations that helped you understand the beginning of the story?' (Sun had a small house and was talking with Water. Sun and Moon started building a bigger house.)

Invite a volunteer to place the Story Elements Board Icon: Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky for beginning on the Story Elements board. Refer to Story Elements Board: Sun and Moon (answers, for teacher reference) as necessary.
Draw students' attention back to the text and read aloud pages 14-22 fluently and without interruption, paying attention to when students show the signal for an important event.

'What did you see and hear that helped you understand the middle of the story?' (Water came to Sun and Moon's house and brought all of his people and animals. Water filled up the house until there was no more room.)
Invite a student volunteer to place the Story Elements board icon for middle on the board.
Draw students' attention back to the text and read the remainder of it, paying attention to when students show the signal for an important event.
'What did you see and hear that helped you understand the end of the story?' (Water overflowed the house. Sun and Moon were forced onto the roof and then up into the sky.)
Invite a student volunteer to place the Story Elements board icon for end on the board.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Cold call a few students to share out their ideas.
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Cold call a few students to share out.
'Can you give an example?' (Responses will vary.)
'Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?' (Responses will vary.)
Move students into the same triads from Lesson 12 and distribute the Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky puppets.

Use the routine established in the first half of the module to review the first learning target and the Working to Become Ethical People anchor chart with students and guide them through the Role-Play protocol for the following pages of Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky. Review the Role-Play Protocol anchor chart as necessary (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of this protocol) and track their progress with the Speaking and Listening Checklist for.
Refocus whole group. Ask students to carry their puppets with respect and care and carefully put them away in the designated place.

Provide specific feedback around students' ability to show respect for their environment. (Example: 'I saw Jin show respect today when he saw a friend waving the puppet in the air and reminded his friend to hold the puppet carefully.')
Tell students that now they are going to write what they know about the major events and central message of Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky, just as they did in Lessons 9 and 11.
Distribute prepared clipboards with Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky response sheets and pencils and follow the same routine established in Lessons 9 and 11 to complete Parts III and IV.
Circulate to support students as they write. Encourage them to use classroom resources (Story Elements board, Word Walls, high-frequency word lists, and alphabet or letter sound combination charts).
When 2 minutes remain, provide students with a time reminder and encourage them to finish up Part IV. Signal all students to stop working through the use of a designated sound.
Collect students' response sheets.

Remind students that the best learning happens when learners check to see how well they are doing and what they can do to be even better. Remind them that this is called 'assessing' and that today they will use the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol to assess their own learning. Remind them that they used this protocol in Module 1 and review as necessary using the Sit, Kneel, Stand Protocol anchor chart. (Refer to the Classroom Protocols document for the full version of this protocol.)
Guide students through the protocol using the learning targets.
Lead the class in a debrief discussion on how the class has rated itself as time allows.
'Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?' (Responses will vary.)

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model singing and moving to the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song and Moon Movement routine; read aloud the story Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky with expression; demonstrate the Sit, Kneel, Stand self-assessment protocol.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: What did you hear that helped you understand the important events from the beginning of the story?
What did you see in the illustrations that helped you understand the beginning of the story?
What did you see and hear that helped you understand the middle of the story?
What did you see and hear that helped you understand the end of the story?
Why do the sun and the moon live in the sky, according to the author, Elphinstone?
What was the central message we learned from Why the Sun and the Moon Live in the Sky?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?
Who can tell us what your classmate said in your own words?

scope.breadth: major story events and central message
scope.depth: detailed retelling and explanation of story events and message

supports.english_language_learners: Provides sentence frames and explicit language support during partner discussions and writing; uses visual aids and gestures during movement and read-aloud; scaffolds partner conversations as needed.
supports.universal_design_udl: Uses multiple modes of engagement including song, movement, visual aids, partner talk, role-play, and writing; provides sentence frames and alternative communication modes; offers physical movement breaks.
supports.below_level_reinforce: Offers explicit prompting and sentence frames during partner discussions and writing; provides additional modeling and visual supports.
supports.above_level_extend: Encourages students to expand partner discussions by giving examples and rephrasing classmates' ideas; invites students to share reasoning and explanations orally.

assessment.method: Self-assessment using the Sit, Kneel, Stand protocol and teacher observation during discussions and role-play

notes: The lesson integrates comprehension of story elements and central message with oral language development, role-play, and writing. It includes supports for English language learners and uses multiple modalities to engage students.

text_complexity.quantitative: read-aloud text, below grade level independent reading band
text_complexity.qualitative: simple story structure with clear beginning, middle, and end; familiar language; supports comprehension with illustrations and repeated phrases
text_complexity.reader_and_task: read-aloud mediation reduces decoding demands; tasks require oral and written retelling and explanation of story events and message
